bibliographic.title: Privacy-by-Design Framework for Large Language Model Chatbots in Urology
bibliographic.venue: International Neurourology Journal (Journal of Korean Continence Society)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Kim, E. J., & Kim, J. (2025). Privacy-by-Design Framework for Large Language Model Chatbots in Urology. International Neurourology Journal. https://doi.org/10.5213/inj.2550274.137

methodology.technology_context: LLM chatbots; foundation models; GPT-4; on-site algorithmic deidentification; federated learning with differential privacy and secure aggregation; secure retrieval-augmented generation with source citation and audit logging; on-premise inference

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed review that directly proposes a privacy-by-design technical and governance framework for safe clinical deployment of LLM chatbots in urology, integrating deidentification, federated learning, secure RAG, audit logging, explainability, and regulatory compliance in a sensitive regulated healthcare domain.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction/objectives text were provided; full review methods, search strategy, included studies, and limitations sections were not available for complete appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on limited excerpt. The review states fourfold objectives including a systematic overview, but detailed review protocol, inclusion criteria, and synthesis methods are not visible in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The framework description is internally coherent and highly relevant to governed LLM chatbot deployment in regulated healthcare, but confidence is moderated because only partial text was supplied and explicit systematic review methodology details were not evidenced.

coding.theme: Privacy-by-design governance for LLM chatbots in regulated clinical settings
coding.subtheme: Urological deployment as test bed for auditable explainable LLM pipelines

synthesis.main_claim: The review proposes a privacy-by-design-based technical and governance framework for safe clinical deployment of LLM chatbots in urology, combining on-site deidentification, federated learning with differential privacy, and secure RAG with source citation and audit logging to create a federated, explainable, and auditable pipeline that preserves data sovereignty and supports regulatory compliance.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an integrated technical-governance architecture for LLM urological chatbots addressing PHI sensitivity, traceability, auditability, explainability, and accountability, positioning urology as a test bed for broader clinical adoption.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text notes structural challenges including PHI privacy/security risks, training data extraction, membership inference attacks, hallucinations, bias, and insufficient source attribution and explainability; full author-stated study limitations are unclear from excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as central evidence for technical-operational conversational governance of LLMs in regulated healthcare, especially privacy-by-design deployment patterns, secure RAG, audit logging, federated learning, and compliance-oriented accountability controls.

evidence.excerpt: This review presents a privacy-by-design–based technical and governance framework for the safe clinical deployment of large language model (LLM) chatbots in urology.
